packageRules.description: Merge an update on its own once CI passes: CI builds and probes every image the update touches, and the merge publishes it. A failed build, probe or tag check blocks the merge, so a person handles only those.
Our own Dockerfiles pin base images by digest.
A followed branch moves with every upstream push; bump it once a week, not on every commit.

OpenMuse's three images share one upstream commit, so they move in one pull request. Their base images ride in the same pull request, on the same weekly schedule: a base image change alone keeps the tag the same, so CI fails until someone bumps revision:. Next to a commit move, the tag changes on its own.
OSIRIS: one image, its own upstream commit, weekly schedule.
opendray: one image, its own upstream commit, weekly schedule.
God's Eye View: one image, its own upstream commit, weekly schedule.
Lichen: one image, its own upstream tag on Tangled, weekly schedule.
Armada: one image, its own upstream tag on GitLab, weekly schedule.
Ditto: one image, its own upstream tag on GitLab, weekly schedule.
Calibre-Web: one image, its own upstream tag, weekly schedule.

customManagers.description: An image that follows an upstream branch: bump the pinned commit when the branch moves. `revision:` must follow `commit:`, so a file with `host:` there does not match. Renovate runs regexes with RE2, which has no lookahead, so this cannot be written as (?!\nhost:).
An image that follows upstream releases: bump the tag and its commit together. `revision:` must follow `commit:` (see the branch rule above).
An image whose upstream is not on GitHub and follows releases: `host:` follows `commit:`. Renovate reads the tags from that host's git URL.
